The Balatro Timeline
Power operators are using sensors and software to dynamically adjust grid safety limits, boosting existing network capacity amid rising AI-driven energy demand (Martha Muir/Financial Times)
A profile of Jensen Huang, whom longtime friends and associates say has an unrelenting ability to make the most of any situation, as he returns as Nvidia's CEO (Erich Schwartzel/Wall Street Journal)
Sweden-based Trustly, which lets merchants accept payments via bank transfers, raised $60M from Nordic Capital and others, taking its total funding to $450M+ (John Reynolds/Tech.eu)
COO Jen Wong says 80%+ of Reddit's monetization comes from logged-in users whose time on the site rises from 5 min/day in year one to 40 min/day by year five (Eleanor Pringle/Fortune)
Embo, which is developing world models for robotics trained on massive amounts of internet video, emerges from stealth with a $110M seed led by a16z (Embo)
Anthropic says Claude doesn't silently sabotage work and that some user reports reflect "overcaution", where Claude clings to self-imposed rules on long tasks (Edwin/@edwinarbus)
How the MATCH Act could backfire by barring ASML from its ~350 immersion scanners in China, letting rivals service and reverse engineer them, and hire its staff (LithoWar)
US insurance giant Allstate has been suffering an outage since November 23, affecting its website and app; the company hasn't said what is causing the outage (Jean Eaglesham/Wall Street Journal)
Some users claim Claude is silently sabotaging projects, especially those involving ML work, but it's hard to prove because models are built to be proactive (Drew Breunig)
Q&A with AI researchers Ege Erdil and Daniel Kokotajlo on the odds of an intelligence explosion before 2029, pausing AI, the US antagonizing China, and more (Dwarkesh Patel/Dwarkesh Podcast)
OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets via a staffer who returned to Apple and "coercing and threatening" suppliers that work with both (Financial Times)
Sources: Verizon is in talks to buy fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium for ~$6B, as part of its goal to expand its network to 50M US homes and businesses (Financial Times)
European Central Bank survey: 44% of employed EU consumers reported using AI weekly at work in August, on par with US peers; 18% used it daily, above US levels (Alexander Weber/Bloomberg)
SAP confirms a cybersecurity incident; report: hackers obtained its staffers' authentication tokens, letting them copy and alter source code stored on GitHub (Eduard Kovacs/SecurityWeek)
The CMA says Meta made changes to Muse's ToS in the UK to reflect the country's consumer law; the terms give users far more protections than in the US (Joseph Bambridge/Politico)
